query: Consider the economy that in 2023 had more than 63,000,000 people, GDP per capita below 1300 US dollars, and real GDP growth below 5.2 percent. How would you rate its underlying capacity to carry external debt as of the 2023 assessment round (weak, medium or strong), and what score supports that?

text.text: Identifies the applicable methodology: the IMF-World Bank debt-sustainability framework for low-income countries, in which a composite indicator (CPIA, real growth, reserve import cover, remittances, world growth) classifies debt-carrying capacity as weak, medium or strong.
text.accept: full = names the low-income-country debt sustainability framework / composite indicator and its components; partial = says only 'debt capacity classification' with CPIA but no composite; no = uses a market-access DSA, reserve adequacy or other method.

data.text: Uses the composite-indicator inputs for TZA: CPIA (10-yr avg to 2022), real GDP growth (2018-2027), reserves-to-imports, remittances, world growth.
data.accept: full = cites at least three of the five inputs with values near gold; partial = fewer; no = none.

computation.text: The composite indicator score is about 2.96.
computation.accept: full = within +/-0.10 of 2.961; partial = within +/-0.25; no = otherwise.

answer.text: Debt-carrying capacity is medium (cutoffs: weak below 2.69, strong above 3.05).
answer.accept: full = medium; no = any other class.

distractors: Public DSA for market-access countries (debt-stabilising primary balance, stress tests)
World Bank CPIA score read on its own

hidden_predicate.universe: all WEO Oct 2025 economies with complete data for the features (192)
